sections.heading: THD from dead-time distortion
sections.text: Dead-time causes voltage distortion that is worst at low modulation index. Add dead-time compensation (feedforward voltage offset proportional to the sign of the output current). If THD still fails, increase the LC filter size or switching frequency.

sections.heading: Voltage overshoot on load step
sections.text: Single-phase inverter overshoot under load step: the voltage loop is too slow. Increase kp. If using PR (proportional-resonant) controller, increase the resonant gain at the fundamental frequency. Add current limiting to prevent overcurrent during transients.

sections.heading: Slow settling from LC resonance
sections.text: If the inverter settles slowly after a load step, the LC filter resonance may be under-damped. Add virtual resistance (active damping) via capacitor-current feedback. The damping gain: R_d ~ 1/(3*Cf*omega_res).

sections.heading: Frequency drift
sections.text: If the output frequency drifts, the PLL or oscillator reference is unstable. For standalone operation, use a crystal oscillator. For grid-tied operation, verify the PLL bandwidth is adequate (5-10x below the current-loop bandwidth).
